title: Operationalising Lifestyle Correction in Routine Outpatient Care: Implementation of the Clinically Supported Lifestyle Correction with Cell Activation Protocol (CSLC-CAP)
content: Background. Non-communicable diseases account for most outpatient visits, long-term prescriptions, and elective surgery, yet practical models for delivering structured lifestyle correction within routine care remain scarce. This report describes the design, delivery, and early dissemination of a doctor-supervised outpatient programme. Programme. The Clinically Supported Lifestyle Correction with Cell Activation Protocol (CSLC-CAP), delivered at a private hospital in Kochi, India, corrects four interdependent lifestyle domains — nutrition, physical and mental activity, rest and sleep, and toxin exposure — through a six-stage pathway from objective baseline assessment to long-term maintenance. Implementation. A small team (consultant doctor, counsellor, activity trainer, pharmacist) delivers a 90-day active phase with daily charting of all four domains, telemedicine follow-up throughout, and serial laboratory and body-composition measurement. Medication is reduced under supervision, guided by test reports in asymptomatic conditions and by symptoms in symptomatic ones. Adaptations include resistance-based activity performed seated or lying down and removal of non-nutritive dietary load. Early insights. Adherence is the rate-limiting step; the first month is the most monitoring-intensive; and benefit persists only while the practice continues, so relapse and restart are built into the pathway. The model is teachable and transferable; formal evaluation is planned.
